analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch adds a paragraph at head lines 595-611 describing a four-row Gated DeltaNet prefill kernel (GatedDeltaPrefill) with packed/rows selection and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED A/B env control. The supplied units are BASE text at lines 798-1637 and are unchanged surrounding context. The added text sits outside the supplied base ranges, so the actual head paragraph is visible only through the patch excerpt. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption, key-handling or billing behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant claims in the new text:
- The kernel is selected only if it reproduces the stock gated_delta_step bit for bit on a fixed probe window, else the stock kernel is used.
- Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows keep the stock kernel.
- Recurrent state used for checkpoint capture is therefore claimed unaffected.

These claims touch T-041 (SSD prefix-cache checkpoint content and keying) and TB-007 (inference engine). The doc asserts bit-exact equivalence, so cached recurrent-state identity and the existing prefix-cache posture (HMAC names, TTL, salt scoping) are claimed unchanged. The implementation is not supplied, so I cannot verify that the probe-and-select logic is bit-exact or that a kernel mismatch could not produce divergent checkpoint state.

The new env var is a performance-only A/B knob. It is a local operator control and not a new trust boundary: the operator already has full control per TB-003. The deadline-qualification environment guard (DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification) already rejects unrecognized DARKBLOOM_* settings, so qualified timing profiles should not be affected by it, but I did not verify that.

No finding. A later pass over the code could confirm the GatedDelta.swift kernel selection and that the new env var is rejected by the qualification environment guard.
